name: Plum blossom (A350-era nose)
description: White, with a lavender swath and a navy band sweeping back from the nose under the cockpit to a point ahead of the wing, and a lilac-gray belly. White fin, lilac at the root rising toward the trailing edge, carrying a big pink plum blossom with red stamens. 'CHINA AIRLINES' in navy serif capitals over the windows, a small red seal after it, a SkyTeam badge behind the cockpit.

areas.name: navy band under the swath, from the nose to a point under the forward door's aft
lilac root, rising aft (a gradient in the paint)

logos.description: The plum blossom (Taiwan's national flower): a five-petalled flower seen face-on, petals pink shading to white toward the middle, a ring of red stamens with dark tips at the center, outlined in thin dark red.
A small red seal (a chop), tall and rounded, just after 'CHINA AIRLINES'.
The SkyTeam badge: a small gray roundel of swirling lines with 'SKYTEAM' round its top, behind the cockpit.

titles.style: Serif capitals with flared, classical strokes, regular weight, widely set over the windows.

notes: Measured on the A350 (B-18906, left side); the A321neo (2022 on) carries the same, and a February 2026 photo of B-18102 still shows it, so no newer scheme was seen on the A321neo. The A350-1000 and 787-10 deliveries weren't found on Commons to check. The fin's lilac is a gradient fading upward, drawn here as one flat area. Older types (737-800, A330, 777, 747F) were delivered in the 1995 plum-blossom scheme without this nose; whether all have been repainted isn't checked. Colors by eye. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on the A321neo (the commonest type, B-18106): the title starts at 0.21 and runs 0.145 of the A321neo (on the A350 it sat at 0.306, run 0.156), the seal right after it; the swath agrees with the A350 drawing except its navy band, which ends in a point about 0.12 back, well short of the lavender's point (the A350 drawing ran it to the end). Its edges are near-straight in the side view and kept as polygons: tracing it against a constant radius near the tapering nose put it too low.
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximation. The plum blossom has been on the fin since 1995; this variant with the lavender and navy nose came with the A350s (from 2016) and the A321neo.
